source.citation: Thompson, D'Arcy W. (1917) On Growth and Form. Cambridge University Press. Ch. XVII 'On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms', pp. 719-777; transformation types pp. 729-731 (Figs. 353-358); Durer heads Fig. 364 (p. 740) and Fig. 366 (p. 742); Camper footnote p. 742.
source.claim_text: Human (and animal) heads/faces and proportions, in the Durer/Camper tradition, are mutually transformable by coordinate deformation; differences of facial angle/proportion are whole-grid deformations.
verbatim_support: p. 729-730: 'we may alter the dimensions of our system, extending it along one or other axis, and so converting each little square into a corresponding and directly proportionate oblong (Fig. 353) ... for the original x and y we have substituted x1 and c*y1, and the equation to our original circle, x^2 + y^2 = a^2, becomes that of the ellipse, x1^2 + c^2 y1^2 = a^2.'
p. 730: '(2) ... the ordinate increases logarithmically, and for y we substitute eps^y ... x becoming eps^x, while y becomes eps^y.'

p. 730: '(3) Our third type is the "simple shear," where the rectangular co-ordinates become "oblique," their axes being inclined to one another at a certain angle omega ... x = xi - eta cot omega, y = eta cosec omega.'

p. 740-741: 'the manner in which the human figure, features, and facial expression are all transformed and modified by slight variations in the relative magnitude of the parts is admirably and copiously illustrated (Fig. 364).'
p. 742: 'Durer was acquainted with these oblique co-ordinates also, and I have copied two illustrative figures from his book (Fig. 366).'

p. 742 footnote: 'It was these very drawings of Durer's that gave to Peter Camper his notion of the "facial angle." ... he saw clearly the essential fact, that the skull varies as a whole, and that the "facial angle" is the index to a general deformation.'

state_variables.(x, y): Cartesian coordinates of a landmark on the reference head (Thompson's 'original net')
state_variables.(x', y'): coordinates of the corresponding landmark in the deformed net
state_variables.omega: angle between the oblique axes (Thompson type 3); omega = 90 deg is the undeformed rectangular net
state_variables.k = -cot(omega): horizontal shear coefficient equivalent to Thompson's oblique net

equations.name: Type 1 proportional (anisotropic) stretch
equations.formula: x' = x,  y' = c*y   (circle x^2+y^2=a^2 -> ellipse x'^2 + (y'/c)^2 = a^2)

equations.name: Type 3 simple shear / oblique coordinates
equations.formula: x = xi - eta*cot(omega),  y = eta*cosec(omega);  equivalently (x', y') = (x + k*y, y) with k = -cot(omega) after rescaling y
equations.source: p. 730, Fig. 357; applied to Durer heads Fig. 366 p. 742

equations.name: Whole-grid (affine) deformation of a landmark configuration
equations.formula: X' = A X + t,  A = [[a11,a12],[a21,a22]] (det A > 0); types 1 and 3 are the sub-families diag(1,c) and shear(k); differences between heads are claimed to lie in this family
equations.source: Ch. XVII general thesis, pp. 719-777; Dürer Figs. 364/366

equations.name: Facial angle as index of a general deformation (Camper footnote)
equations.formula: for a facial line of direction (dx, dy): tan(phi') = (dx + k*dy)/dy = tan(phi) + k  — a shear k changes the inclination of EVERY vertical line by the same amount

mathematical_model.boundary_conditions: Landmarks are 2-D points on the mid-sagittal soft-tissue profile; the transformation is global (one A, t per head pair); no local (landmark-specific) displacement is permitted under the claim.

parameter_regime.durer_fig366_estimate: measured on the IA scan by Hough transform (see script, Pass 2)
parameter_regime.note: Thompson's tapir-toe example uses omega = 50 deg (p. 741); Durer's heads are milder
ox -> sheep cannon bone uses x' = 2x/3 (p. 730), i.e. c = 1.5 along the bone axis
logarithmic stretch base (type 2), small values only

test_statistics.warp_family_fit: per ordered specimen pair, least-squares similarity (4 dof), anisotropic (5 dof, rotation+two scales) and full affine / Durer grid (6 dof) fits of landmark set A onto B; residual RMSE in centroid-size units; LOO-CV residual
test_statistics.variance_explained: R_affine = 1 - SS(affine)/SS(similarity): fraction of non-similarity shape difference captured by the whole-grid deformation
test_statistics.noise_floor: landmark re-detection RMSE under image perturbation (rescale 0.85/1.15, blur sigma 1 px)
test_statistics.facial_angle_link: Pearson r between fitted shear k_AB and the measured change in profile inclination / convexity angle (E5)

empirical_claims_to_test.claim: Inter-individual differences in human facial profile are captured by a single whole-grid (affine: stretch + shear) deformation
empirical_claims_to_test.prediction_if_true: affine residual RMSE <= ~1.5 x landmark noise floor for most pairs; R_affine high
empirical_claims_to_test.prediction_if_false: affine residual far above noise floor; local features (nose, lips, chin) need independent change

empirical_claims_to_test.claim: Facial angle differences are the index of the shear component of that deformation (Camper footnote)
empirical_claims_to_test.prediction_if_true: fitted k correlates tightly (|r| > 0.8) with measured inclination change, slope ~1 in tan units
empirical_claims_to_test.prediction_if_false: weak correlation; angle changes arise from local features

empirical_claims_to_test.claim: The affine family is not trivially satisfied: a scrambled-correspondence / local-perturbation control must fail
